**Class** in the `Latiprimere.Ipp` namespace, from the [Latiprimere.Ipp](/docs/reference/#latiprimereipp) package.

```csharp
public sealed class IppNetworkOptions
```

Configures printing directly to IPP network printers, without CUPS or the Windows spooler.

## Constructors

```csharp
public IppNetworkOptions()
```

## Properties

### AddressStorePath

```csharp
public string? AddressStorePath { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets a file in which to remember where each printer found on the network was last seen, so it is found there after the application restarts even if it doesn't answer the search, as a sleeping printer may not. Defaults to `null`: remembered only while the print system lives.

The file is JSON, read when the print system is created and written whenever a printer's address changes. A missing or unreadable file means starting with nothing remembered, and is logged, never an error; so is a file that can't be written. A remembered address is used only while the printer there still reports the UUID it announced.

Keep it where only the application can write: an address in it counts as a printer found on the network, so it may be looked up by its `ipp:` URI identifier as well as by name.

### AllowAnyPrinterUri

```csharp
public bool AllowAnyPrinterUri { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets a value indicating whether a printer identifier may name any IPP URI (`ipp:ipp://host/path`), not only one in [IppNetworkOptions.PrinterUris](/docs/reference/latiprimere-ipp/ippnetworkoptions/#printeruris) or of a printer found on the network. Defaults to `false`.

Looking a printer up by URI connects to whatever host and port the URI names. When identifiers can come from outside the application, such as from a web request, allowing any URI would let others make it connect to internal services (server-side request forgery). Turn this on only when every identifier the application looks up is trusted. Otherwise a lookup of an unlisted URI finds no printer, without connecting.

### AllowPlainIppAfterIpps

```csharp
public bool AllowPlainIppAfterIpps { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets a value indicating whether a printer found on the network may be reached over plain IPP after it has been reached over IPPS, when its IPPS address stops working. Defaults to `false`.

By default, once a printer found on the network has been reached over IPPS with a trusted certificate, while a certificate is pinned or [IppNetworkOptions.ServerCertificateValidationCallback](/docs/reference/latiprimere-ipp/ippnetworkoptions/#servercertificatevalidationcallback) is set, it is refused with a [PrintException](/docs/reference/latiprimere-abstractions/printexception/) rather than reached over plain IPP, if its IPPS address stops answering, its certificate is no longer trusted, or its name is announced with only a plain address. Any of those could be a device on the network forcing its jobs onto plain IPP, where they can be read. A printer that has never been reached over IPPS falls back either way.

Set it to `true` to fall back as before, as for printers whose certificates change often and whose documents needn't be kept private. The fallback is logged as a warning. It has no effect while [IppNetworkOptions.RequireEncryption](/docs/reference/latiprimere-ipp/ippnetworkoptions/#requireencryption) is set, which never allows plain IPP. Whether each printer was reached over IPPS is remembered either way, so turning it off again protects them at once.

### AllowRememberedAddressWithoutUuid

```csharp
public bool AllowRememberedAddressWithoutUuid { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets a value indicating whether a printer found on the network that announced a UUID may be used at its remembered address when the printer there reports no UUID at all. Defaults to `false`.

Looking a printer up by name tries the address it was last seen at first, and uses it only if the printer there is the same: it must report, as `printer-uuid`, the UUID it announced. By default, one that reports no UUID isn't taken on trust, as another device at the address could pass by leaving it out; the network is searched for the name instead, which takes a little longer.

Set it to `true` to take such a printer on trust, as before, for older printers that announce a UUID but don't report `printer-uuid` and that would otherwise be searched for at every lookup. A printer that reports a different UUID is never used there, and one that announced none is always taken on trust.

### BusyRetryDuration

```csharp
public TimeSpan BusyRetryDuration { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets how long to keep resending a job that a printer turns away because it is busy with another (IPP status `server-error-busy`). Printers that take one job at a time do this. Defaults to [IppNetworkOptions.DefaultBusyRetryDuration](/docs/reference/latiprimere-ipp/ippnetworkoptions/#defaultbusyretryduration); [TimeSpan.Zero](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.timespan.zero) sends each job once.

The waits between attempts start at one second and double, up to 15 seconds, as each attempt sends the whole document again. Only documents in seekable streams can be resent; others fail on the first busy answer. When the time runs out, the busy error is thrown as a [PrintException](/docs/reference/latiprimere-abstractions/printexception/).

**Exceptions**

- [ArgumentOutOfRangeException](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentoutofrangeexception): The value is negative.

### ConnectTimeout

```csharp
public TimeSpan ConnectTimeout { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets the longest wait for a connection to a printer to open. Defaults to [IppNetworkOptions.DefaultConnectTimeout](/docs/reference/latiprimere-ipp/ippnetworkoptions/#defaultconnecttimeout), 10 seconds; without a limit, an address with nothing behind it can take about 21 seconds to fail on Windows.

It covers opening the connection only, not waiting for an answer. When it runs out, the request fails with a [PrintException](/docs/reference/latiprimere-abstractions/printexception/).

**Exceptions**

- [ArgumentOutOfRangeException](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentoutofrangeexception): The value is not positive, or is longer than about 24 days.

### Credentials

```csharp
public NetworkCredential? Credentials { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets the user name and password sent to every printer over IPPS, or `null`, the default, to send none. [IppNetworkOptions.PrinterCredentials](/docs/reference/latiprimere-ipp/ippnetworkoptions/#printercredentials) overrides it for particular printers.

They are sent with every request, as HTTP Basic authentication, and only over IPPS, never in clear text. A printer that asks for a password over plain IPP is refused with a [PrintAuthenticationException](/docs/reference/latiprimere-abstractions/printauthenticationexception/) saying to use its `ipps://` address. The [NetworkCredential.Domain](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.net.networkcredential.domain) is not used.

Every printer reached over IPPS receives them, once its certificate is trusted. While they are set, a certificate the system trusts is enough only for printers configured in [IppNetworkOptions.PrinterUris](/docs/reference/latiprimere-ipp/ippnetworkoptions/#printeruris) or [IppNetworkOptions.PrinterCredentials](/docs/reference/latiprimere-ipp/ippnetworkoptions/#printercredentials): anyone on the network can announce a printer at a host whose certificate a public authority issued, so a printer found on the network must have its certificate pinned in [IppNetworkOptions.TrustedCertificateFingerprints](/docs/reference/latiprimere-ipp/ippnetworkoptions/#trustedcertificatefingerprints) or accepted by [IppNetworkOptions.ServerCertificateValidationCallback](/docs/reference/latiprimere-ipp/ippnetworkoptions/#servercertificatevalidationcallback). Until then its IPPS address is refused, and it is reached over plain IPP, without them, if it announces that too and [IppNetworkOptions.RequireEncryption](/docs/reference/latiprimere-ipp/ippnetworkoptions/#requireencryption) isn't set. To keep a password to one printer, use [IppNetworkOptions.PrinterCredentials](/docs/reference/latiprimere-ipp/ippnetworkoptions/#printercredentials).

### DiscoveryDuration

```csharp
public TimeSpan DiscoveryDuration { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets how long to listen for printer announcements each time printers are listed. A lookup by name that has to search the network waits at most this long, and usually much less, as it stops when the printer answers; it only searches when the printer's last known address doesn't answer.

**Exceptions**

- [ArgumentOutOfRangeException](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentoutofrangeexception): The value is negative, or is longer than about 24 days.

### EnableDiscovery

```csharp
public bool EnableDiscovery { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets a value indicating whether to find printers on the local network with DNS-SD (Bonjour/mDNS) when listing printers. Defaults to `true`. Looking up a printer by its name identifier (`ipp:dnssd:`) always searches the network, whatever this setting.

### MaxRenderDpi

```csharp
public int? MaxRenderDpi { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets the highest resolution, in dots per inch, a PDF is rendered at when it is sent as raster to a printer that can't take PDF. Defaults to `null`: the printer's default resolution.

A printer that doesn't take PDF is sent its pages as images, in a format of [IppNetworkOptions.RasterFormats](/docs/reference/latiprimere-ipp/ippnetworkoptions/#rasterformats), at one of the resolutions it lists, which needs a PDF rasteriser such as Latiprimere.Rendering.Pdfium. Its default is used when it has one and it is within this limit; otherwise the highest it lists within the limit and 600 dpi. If it lists none that low, its lowest is used. Resolutions above 2400 dpi are never used, whatever this limit.

Lower resolutions render and upload faster: an A4 page at 600 dpi is four times the pixels of one at 300 dpi. Small text and fine lines are softer.

**Exceptions**

- [ArgumentOutOfRangeException](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentoutofrangeexception): The value is zero or negative.

### PrinterCertificateFingerprints

```csharp
public IDictionary<Uri, string> PrinterCertificateFingerprints { get; }
```

Gets the SHA-256 fingerprints of printer certificates to trust over IPPS only at one printer's address, by printer URI, such as `ipps://192.168.1.20/ipp/print`. They are matched by the URI's host, and written as in [IppNetworkOptions.TrustedCertificateFingerprints](/docs/reference/latiprimere-ipp/ippnetworkoptions/#trustedcertificatefingerprints).

A certificate pinned here is trusted only at that host, whatever name it carries, so the same certificate presented anywhere else is refused. A printer found on the network is reached at the address it announces, so pin it by that address; if it gets a new one, its certificate is refused there until it is pinned again.

### PrinterCredentials

```csharp
public IDictionary<Uri, NetworkCredential> PrinterCredentials { get; }
```

Gets the user names and passwords of particular printers, by printer URI, such as `ipps://192.168.1.20/ipp/print`. They are matched by host and port, and sent only over IPPS, as [IppNetworkOptions.Credentials](/docs/reference/latiprimere-ipp/ippnetworkoptions/#credentials) are.

### PrinterUris

```csharp
public IList<Uri> PrinterUris { get; }
```

Gets the URIs of printers to list even if they don't announce themselves, such as `ipp://192.168.1.20/ipp/print`.

### RasterFormats

```csharp
public IList<IppRasterFormat> RasterFormats { get; }
```

Gets the raster formats a PDF may be rendered into for a printer that can't take PDF, in the order they're tried: by default PWG raster, then Apple raster, then PCLm.

The first the printer lists is used. A printer that takes PDF is always sent the PDF. Reorder the list to prefer a format, or leave one out so it's never sent, as for a printer that handles one badly. Empty, a printer that can't take PDF is refused PDFs with a [NotSupportedException](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.notsupportedexception), as without a rasteriser.

PCLm is a PDF of image strips, which Mopria printers take; Latiprimere compresses its strips with Flate or run-length encoding, whichever the printer prefers.

### RequireEncryption

```csharp
public bool RequireEncryption { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets a value indicating whether every request goes over an encrypted connection (IPPS), never plain IPP. Defaults to `false`.

When `true`, a printer found on the network is reached only at its IPPS address: one that announces none, or whose certificate isn't trusted, is refused with a [PrintException](/docs/reference/latiprimere-abstractions/printexception/) rather than reached over plain IPP, where anyone able to watch the network could read the documents. Looking up an `ipp://` URI is refused the same way, without connecting, and an `ipp://` URI in [IppNetworkOptions.PrinterUris](/docs/reference/latiprimere-ipp/ippnetworkoptions/#printeruris) throws [ArgumentException](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentexception) when the print system is created.

Without it, a printer found on the network is still never reached over plain IPP once it has been reached over IPPS with a trusted certificate, while a certificate is pinned or the callback is set, so a device that answers in its place, or blocks its IPPS port, can't make it fall back; unless [IppNetworkOptions.AllowPlainIppAfterIpps](/docs/reference/latiprimere-ipp/ippnetworkoptions/#allowplainippafteripps) is set.

### ServerCertificateValidationCallback

```csharp
public RemoteCertificateValidationCallback? ServerCertificateValidationCallback { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets the check of a printer's certificate that neither the system trusts nor [IppNetworkOptions.TrustedCertificateFingerprints](/docs/reference/latiprimere-ipp/ippnetworkoptions/#trustedcertificatefingerprints) pins, or `null`, the default, to refuse it.

Return `true` only for a certificate you have checked, for example by its fingerprint: anyone able to intercept the connection could otherwise read the documents and any password.

### TrustedCertificateFingerprints

```csharp
public IList<string> TrustedCertificateFingerprints { get; }
```

Gets the SHA-256 fingerprints of printer certificates to trust over IPPS (`ipps://`), in hexadecimal, with or without colons between the bytes, such as `3A:7F:…`.

Printers nearly always present a certificate they made themselves, which no computer trusts, so a printer's IPPS address is refused until its certificate is trusted. A certificate pinned here is trusted whatever name it carries, as printers' certificates rarely name the address they're reached at. The [PrintException](/docs/reference/latiprimere-abstractions/printexception/) for a refused certificate gives its fingerprint; check it against the one the printer's web page shows before adding it.

Once a certificate is pinned, or [IppNetworkOptions.ServerCertificateValidationCallback](/docs/reference/latiprimere-ipp/ippnetworkoptions/#servercertificatevalidationcallback) is set, a printer found on the network that announces both addresses is reached over IPPS, and over plain IPP only if its certificate isn't trusted and it has never been reached over IPPS before. Set [IppNetworkOptions.RequireEncryption](/docs/reference/latiprimere-ipp/ippnetworkoptions/#requireencryption) to never reach one over plain IPP.

A pinned certificate is trusted at any address. Printers of one model sometimes share a certificate made at the factory, which would then be trusted on every one of them; to trust a certificate only at one printer's address, pin it in [IppNetworkOptions.PrinterCertificateFingerprints](/docs/reference/latiprimere-ipp/ippnetworkoptions/#printercertificatefingerprints) instead.

### UploadStallTimeout

```csharp
public TimeSpan UploadStallTimeout { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets the longest a printer may go without taking any more of a job's document, or without answering once it has been sent it all. Defaults to [IppNetworkOptions.DefaultUploadStallTimeout](/docs/reference/latiprimere-ipp/ippnetworkoptions/#defaultuploadstalltimeout), 5 minutes; [Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.threading.timeout.infinitetimespan) waits as long as the printer takes.

It limits a lack of progress, not the whole upload: a large job to a printer that reads it only as fast as it prints takes as long as it needs while the printer keeps reading, and the time spent rendering a PDF sent as raster isn't counted. A printer that stops reading partway, such as one that jams, sleeps or loses its network connection without closing it, would otherwise hold the submission until the caller's cancellation token, if any, cancels it.

When it runs out, the submission fails with a [PrintException](/docs/reference/latiprimere-abstractions/printexception/) saying whether the printer stopped taking the document or didn't answer once it was sent it all. The job isn't sent again: the printer may already have printed some of it. Allow for a printer that pauses before it starts, to warm up or clean its heads, and between pages, as an inkjet printing on both sides does while the ink dries.

**Exceptions**

- [ArgumentOutOfRangeException](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentoutofrangeexception): The value is not positive, other than [Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.threading.timeout.infinitetimespan), or is longer than about 24 days.

### UserName

```csharp
public string? UserName { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets the user name sent with requests as `requesting-user-name`, which printers list jobs under. When `null`, the current operating-system user name is used.

It isn't a login, and printers don't check it. For a printer that asks for a user name and password, set [IppNetworkOptions.Credentials](/docs/reference/latiprimere-ipp/ippnetworkoptions/#credentials) or [IppNetworkOptions.PrinterCredentials](/docs/reference/latiprimere-ipp/ippnetworkoptions/#printercredentials).

### ValidateJobs

```csharp
public bool ValidateJobs { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets whether to ask a printer to check a job's attributes with Validate-Job before sending the document. Defaults to `true`.

A printer refuses a job with an option it can't carry out, such as a paper size it doesn't have. With this on, it refuses before the document is uploaded, with a [PrintException](/docs/reference/latiprimere-abstractions/printexception/) whose [PrintException.NativeErrorCode](/docs/reference/latiprimere-abstractions/printexception/#nativeerrorcode) is the IPP status, rather than after. It costs one short request per job, and is only sent to printers that list Validate-Job among their operations. A printer too busy to answer it gets the job anyway.
